720	A woman is Hei: she takes the male's point, the single drop, and in nine months forms
721	a person with hands and feet.
722	With a head, hands, feet, a whole body from top to bottom.
723	The male's power is to give the beginning of the continuation, to start it, to give the point.
724	The woman's power is to give the whole.
725	The woman's power is to break the whole down into details.
726	So a man is in the yod, a woman in the hei: that is her trait.
727	Now we begin to understand the problem here.
728	Avraham Avinu first of all must have children, and second, he must be the father of a multitude of nations.
729	He must carry the faith on to everyone in the world.
730	But he has no hei, no added measure of fertility, no added measure of expansion.
731	He has an alef, he has many ideas, and he has a bet, he has a great many big ideas.
732	But a hei, he does not have.
733	An added measure of expansion, of binah, of continuity, of influence.
734	The ability to come down below, to build a whole structure that you can pass on.
735	This Avraham Avinu does not have.
736	So a hei must be added to him.
737	So that he can become, from Avram to Avraham, the father of a multitude of nations.
738	He lacks the hei of expansion.
739	With Sarah, it is even greater.
740	Not only does Sarah not have a hei, she has a yod.
741	What is a yod?
742	A yod is another male letter.
743	One that belongs to the male, not to the woman at all.
744	For her, the yod does damage.
745	We asked: why not call her Sariah?
746	It's prettier.
747	Serayah, a great Jew of the previous generation, Serayah Devlitsky.
748	He was an immense Torah scholar, Serayah Devlitsky.
749	Why would they not call her Serayah?
750	Sar-yod-kei, Sarah, yod-kei, how beautiful.
751	In a woman, the yod is harmful.
752	In a woman, the yod does not belong in the name.
753	So HaShem removes the yod and gives her the hei, which is the woman's ability to create, to take
754	the continuity from Avraham
755	and form from it the expansion, in length and breadth, of the extra binah: to create the pregnancy.
756	So what is the point here?
757	It is not just swapping letters.
758	It is not that one could just as well put a final mem.
759	It is a letter that belongs to fertility.
760	Based on this, the Rebbe Maharash once said something very special.
761	Rachel does not give birth.
762	Rachel is barren for many years, and she weeps bitterly, she does not give birth.
763	And then an idea comes to her.
764	What idea?
765	Perhaps I will take my maidservant Bilhah, perhaps I will be built up through her.
766	She says: I will take Bilhah so that she gives birth, and I will be built up through her.
767	How will you build your family?
768	The child will be called the maidservant's, not yours.
769	How will you be built up through the maidservant?
770	So we must say that in those days the maidservant did serve as a surrogate.
771	The children the maidservant bore belonged to the mistress.
772	So it is as if Rachel says in despair: Bilhah will give birth, and I will be built up through her.
773	But no, said the Rebbe Maharash, listen to this brilliance.
774	No, not at all.
775	She is saying: in the merit of Bilhah, I too will merit to give birth.
776	Why?
777	Rachel is the only one of the Matriarchs who lacks a hei in her name: Sarah, Rivkah, Leah. Rachel is the only one without a hei.
778	With no hei she cannot give birth. What will she do?
779	She says: Bilhah has two heis, so one will be for her and one for me. Perhaps I will be built up
780	through Bilhah, I will receive the abundance so that I too can give birth. The idea, then, is that a person needs the
781	specific letter that gives the specific energy for what he needs in that matter. We begin to understand
782	what a responsibility this is for parents. What do I know?
783	I know which name is good, which name is bad.
784	So what are we told?
785	Go on the safe side.
786	Go for names that have already succeeded.
787	Be called Rabbi Meir, be called Rabbi Yehudah, be called Rabbi Yosei.
788	Someone already ran the experiment.
789	And you saw that it works?
790	You saw that it is a channel?
791	I do not know what Yosei is.
792	But I know that it is a channel that brings abundance.
793	So bring this channel.
794	Why should you take risks?
795	Bring new names, when you yourself do not know what they mean.
796	Here you have a name on which someone already ran the experiment.
797	And likewise the opposite: the Gemara says terrible things, it is forbidden even to…
798	that the name… The famine was terrible, and they ate the flesh of their children, a terrible curse was fulfilled, may HaShem have mercy,
799	there was a rich, pampered woman, and they ate the flesh of their children.
800	The Gemara says that the child was called Doeg.
801	The Gemara says: so see what came of him.
802	At the beginning they called him Doeg.
803	See where he ended up: call him a name of worry, see what mazal it brought.
804	That is to say, the Chatam Sofer says: how could…
805	the father of Korach, Yitzhar, right?
806	Korach son of…?
807	Yitzhar, right?
808	He says: how could Yitzhar call his son by the name Korach?
809	After all, Korach is among the chiefs of Esav.
810	How did he give him such a name?
811	Look, just on our own.
812	How does the Chatam Sofer say such a thing about a descendant of…?
813	And so says the Chatam Sofer.
814	How did he call him Korach?
815	A child of Esav.
816	They are among the chiefs of Esav, how does he give him such a name?
817	That is to say, you see that one must understand: a name that has already been proven not to be ours, one must be very
818	careful of it, as opposed to a name that is ours.
819	So, all right?
820	So it has already been proven to be a good name, you do not need to understand the combination.
821	Here, the prophecy given to parents is to connect to a name they love from the basket of all the biblical or Talmudic names,
822	and to choose a good name that is comfortable for them.
823	How far do these things go?
824	I want to tell a story with the people involved.
825	Does everyone know Rabbi Adin Even-Israel?
826	The commentator on the Talmud, here too are his books, everywhere Rabbi Adin Even-Israel, a Jew who merited and was obligated
827	to produce endlessly, to explain the Torah, to explain the Tanakh, to explain the Rambam, to explain the Mishnah, everything.
828	Whoever looked at his books knows that he has another name.
829	Rabbi Adin Even-Israel, Steinsaltz.
830	Right, in parentheses, Steinsaltz.
831	How did he go from Steinsaltz to Even-Israel?
832	A truly amazing story.
833	He passed before the Rebbe in the month of Cheshvan 5750, exactly 36 years ago, and suddenly the Rebbe gives him a dollar for tzedakah.
834	And the Rebbe says something that, as far as I know, happened only once in all of history.
835	The Rebbe says to him: look, the name Steinsaltz in Yiddish means a salt stone.
836	A salt stone is a name that expresses bitterness, it is not a good name.
837	You should change it. As far as I know, this is the only time the Rebbe said such a thing.
838	In Igrot Kodesh, when people ask the Rebbe to add a name, to change a name as we said, the Rebbe turns it down.
839	He says: without an important reason, the fact that a person has no mazal, has no luck, cannot find an apartment, is not a reason to change a name.
